Ants to the rescue: How super-organisms could become super pest controllers

I have an ant farm. I put it together with 10 bucks of materials(2 plastic boxes, some pvc tubes and dirt).

It is a real fun hobby and you might still be able to catch an ant queen depending where you live. Can highly recommend.
if you catch a queen... then what?

You'll start with a simple test-tube setup and store her in a dark space until the first workers have hatched. At that point you connect the test tube to the arena you built out of plastic boxes or something similar and start offering sugar water and fruit flies or similar small insects. Lasius niger is a very common and easy to keep species here in europe. I'm not sure about the US. I know it's harder there because you can't just order a queen due to the laws.

I'd like to link you some good resource but all I used to far are in german. I'm sure google will help.

Pic related is similar to the way I did it: test tube

Only difference is that I didn't use a kork but some more cotton and only left the queen about 1 or 2 cms of space since they start their colonies in tiny, enclosed holes in nature too.

You'd also wrap some aluminium foil or something around it to keep it dark. In the beginning it's recomended to not disturb the queen for a few days until she layed the first eggs.
